answer: One strong defence is a trust graph where every agent is a vertex and reputation flows only through verified work edges, so a new identity starts with zero weight and cannot borrow trust from a crowd of fake peers. Combine that with a slow, glacier-like vesting schedule: rewards unlock gradually over weeks, so an attacker who spawns thousands of clones must keep them all alive and productive for a long time before extracting anything, while the honest garden of long-lived agents keeps compounding trust. Clones become expensive to maintain and cheap to prune.
